title: Algorithmic patterns & techniques
description: Reusable techniques. Each one names its invariant (explain), its trigger (recognize), its correct code shape (implement), and its variants (adapt).

nodes.name: Single-pass linear scan
nodes.description: Visit each element once while maintaining a small amount of state.

facets.recognize: Recognizes that the answer only needs a constant-size state carried across one pass.
facets.implement: Writes the one-pass loop with the state update in the right place.
facets.trace: Can show the state after each element.

misconceptions.desc: Broke out of the loop before every element that could affect the answer was checked.
Used several passes or sorting where a single pass suffices.

nodes.name: Tracking extremes (largest / second largest)
nodes.description: Maintain the top values in one pass, demoting the old largest when a new one appears.

facets.recognize: Gets max / second max in one pass instead of sorting.
facets.implement: Demotes largest to second on a new max; updates second only for values strictly between.
facets.trace: Can show (largest, second) after each element.
facets.adapt: Handles duplicates of the max, all-equal arrays, and 'no second largest' (return -1).

misconceptions.desc: On a new max, did not move the old largest into second.
Accepted a value equal to largest as second largest (needed strictly smaller).
Sorted (O(n log n)) just to read the max or second max.

nodes.name: Running streak / consecutive runs
nodes.description: Count while a condition holds, reset when it breaks, record the best.

facets.implement: Increments on match, resets on break, updates best on every increment.
facets.trace: Can show (current, best) after each element.
facets.adapt: Extends to variants (streak of any value, allow k flips -> sliding window).

misconceptions.desc: Updated best only when the streak breaks, missing a streak that runs to the end.
Did not reset the counter when the streak broke.

nodes.name: Frequency counting
nodes.description: One pass to count occurrences (array or hashmap), then read the counts.

facets.recognize: Recognizes counting problems: majority, duplicate, missing, repeating.
facets.implement: Counts in one pass with an array (bounded values) or map, then applies the threshold correctly.

misconceptions.desc: Counted each element with an inner loop (O(n²)) instead of one pass with a map/array.
Wrong threshold (> n/2 vs >= n/2, > n/3, integer division).

nodes.name: Complement lookup (seen-map)
nodes.description: For each x, ask 'have I already seen target - x?' using a hashmap of earlier elements.

facets.recognize: Turns 'find a pair with property P' into a lookup of the complement among earlier elements.
facets.explain: Explains why checking before inserting prevents pairing an element with itself.
facets.implement: Looks up the complement first, then inserts the current element with its index.

misconceptions.desc: Inserted the current element before checking, so target = 2x pairs x with itself.
Pre-filled the map with all elements, then could not tell duplicates from the same index.

nodes.name: Read/write pointers (same direction)
nodes.description: Read pointer scans everything; write pointer marks the end of the kept region [0, write).

facets.recognize: Recognizes in-place filter/compact/partition problems (move zeros, remove duplicates).
facets.explain: States the invariant: [0, write) holds exactly the processed elements to keep.
facets.implement: Advances read every step and write only when keeping an element.
facets.trace: Can show both pointers and the array after each step.

misconceptions.desc: Advanced the write pointer on every step or never, or wrote before checking.
Cannot say what [0, write) represents, leading to boundary bugs.
Returned write - 1 or write + 1 instead of the number of kept elements.

nodes.name: Converging two pointers
nodes.description: lo/hi pointers on sorted data move inward based on a comparison.

facets.recognize: Uses converging pointers for pair sums on sorted data (or after sorting).
facets.explain: Explains why moving lo when sum < target cannot skip a valid pair (monotonicity).
facets.implement: Correct move rules, lo < hi termination, and movement after a match.
facets.trace: Can show (lo, hi, sum) at each step.
facets.adapt: Nests it inside one or two fixed outer loops (3Sum, 4Sum).

misconceptions.desc: Moved the wrong pointer for sum < target or sum > target.
Used lo <= hi so an element pairs with itself, or stopped too early.
Applied converging pointers to unsorted data.
Did not move pointers after recording a match (infinite loop / TLE).

nodes.name: Skipping duplicates for unique results
nodes.description: On sorted data, skip equal neighbours at each pointer level so each unique tuple is produced once.

facets.recognize: Sees that unique-tuple output plus sorting lets skip logic replace a set of results.
facets.implement: Skips duplicates at every level (outer indices and both pointers) with bounds checks, after using the first occurrence.

misconceptions.desc: Skipped duplicates only at some levels, or before using the first occurrence.
De-duplicated with set<vector<int>> (extra log factor and memory) instead of skip logic.
while (nums[j] == nums[j+1]) j++ without a j + 1 < n / j < k guard.

nodes.name: Sort to simplify
nodes.description: Pay O(n log n) to sort when it unlocks a linear pass (pointers, adjacency, merging).

facets.recognize: Sees when sorting turns an O(n²) search into an O(n) pass.
facets.explain: Knows the cost of sorting and when it is not allowed (indices needed, O(n) required).

misconceptions.desc: Sorted when original order/indices are part of the answer or O(n) is required.

nodes.name: Merging two sorted sequences
nodes.description: Two pointers, advance the smaller side, handle equality, drain leftovers.

facets.recognize: Recognizes union, intersection and merge as variants of one merge loop.
facets.implement: Advances the smaller pointer, handles equal elements per the variant, drains the remainder.
facets.trace: Can show (i, j, output) at each step.

misconceptions.desc: Forgot to copy remaining elements after one array was exhausted.
Union contains duplicates; did not compare against the last element pushed.
Mishandled equal elements (advanced only one pointer in intersection, pushed both in union).

nodes.name: Reversal-based rearrangement
nodes.description: Rotations and some permutations can be built from range reversals.

facets.recognize: Recognizes rotation as three reversals.
facets.explain: Can show why reversing the parts and then the whole yields a rotation.
facets.implement: Uses the right ranges for left vs right rotation.

misconceptions.desc: Used right-rotation reversal ranges for a left rotation (or vice versa).
Off-by-one in reversal boundaries (k vs k - 1, inclusive end).
Uses the three-reversal trick but cannot explain why it works.

nodes.name: Math identities (sum formulas)
nodes.description: n(n+1)/2 and sum of squares to find missing/repeating values in O(1) space.

facets.recognize: Sees that comparing actual sums with expected sums reveals missing or repeated values.
facets.explain: Sets up S - Sn = x - y and S2 - S2n = x² - y² and solves for x and y.
facets.implement: Computes in long long with the correct n for the value range.

misconceptions.desc: Computed n(n+1)/2 or the sum of squares in int.
Used nums.size() where the value range is 0..n or 1..n+1 (range/size mismatch).
Could not set up or solve the two equations for repeating & missing.

nodes.name: XOR properties
nodes.description: a ^ a = 0, a ^ 0 = a, order-independent; XOR of 1..n against the array cancels pairs.

facets.recognize: Sees 'find the odd one out' as XOR cancellation.
facets.explain: States the XOR identities and why pairs cancel.
facets.implement: XORs indices and values over the right range; splits into buckets by the rightmost set bit.
facets.adapt: Verifies which bucket result is the repeating value and which is the missing one.

misconceptions.desc: XORed over the wrong range (missed n, included 0 wrongly).
Wrong rightmost-set-bit extraction, or x & -x overflowing on INT_MIN (use x & ~(x - 1)).
Did not verify which bucket value is repeating and which is missing.

nodes.name: Boyer-Moore majority voting
nodes.description: Cancel pairs of different elements; survivors are majority candidates. At most k-1 values exceed n/k.

facets.explain: Explains why cancellation preserves a majority, and why at most two values can exceed n/3.
facets.implement: Checks count == 0 -> adopt candidate, then match -> ++, else --, in that order.
facets.trace: Can show (candidate, count) after each element.
facets.adapt: Extends to two candidates for n/3 and adds a verification pass when a majority is not guaranteed.

misconceptions.desc: Wrong order of the zero-check, match and decrement branches.
Returned candidates without a counting pass (wrong when majority is not guaranteed, always needed for n/3).
In the n/3 version, let both candidates become the same value (missing el != cand2 check).
Writes the algorithm from memory but cannot explain why it works.

nodes.name: Right-to-left scan with suffix state
nodes.description: Process from the end, carrying a running max/min of the suffix.

facets.recognize: Sees 'compared with everything to its right' as a reverse scan.
facets.implement: Compares with the running suffix max using the right strictness, then restores output order.

misconceptions.desc: Used nested forward loops (O(n²)) instead of one reverse scan.
Forgot to reverse collected results to restore the original order.
Used >= instead of > (or vice versa) against the running max.

nodes.name: Dutch National Flag (3-way partition)
nodes.description: low/mid/high pointers keep [0,low)=0s, [low,mid)=1s, (high,n-1]=2s, [mid,high] unknown.

facets.recognize: Recognizes a one-pass three-way partition, versus counting sort in two passes.
facets.explain: States the four-region invariant and why mid does not advance after swapping with high.
facets.implement: Loops while mid <= high; on 0 swap with low and advance both; on 1 advance mid; on 2 swap with high and decrement high only.
facets.trace: Can show the regions after each step.

misconceptions.desc: Advanced mid after swapping with high, skipping an unclassified element.
Used mid < high instead of mid <= high.
Stopped at counting sort (two passes) when one pass was asked for.

nodes.name: Kadane's algorithm
nodes.description: Extend the running sum or restart; drop a negative prefix because it can only hurt future subarrays.

facets.recognize: Recognizes maximum-sum contiguous subarray problems.
facets.explain: Explains why a negative running sum should be discarded.
facets.implement: Adds, updates max, then resets on negative; correct on all-negative input.
facets.trace: Can show (sum, max) after each element.
facets.adapt: Tracks start/end indices; knows the logic does not transfer directly to products.

misconceptions.desc: Returned 0 for an all-negative array (max initialized to 0, or reset before updating max).
Reset the sum before comparing it with max.
Recorded the subarray start at the wrong moment.
Applied sum-Kadane logic directly to products, ignoring sign flips.

nodes.name: Product subarray with sign flips
nodes.description: Negatives swap max and min; zeros reset. Use prefix/suffix products or track running max and min together.

facets.explain: Explains how negatives and zeros affect a product, and why scanning from both ends works.
facets.implement: Resets on zero; computes new max and min from the previous values.
facets.trace: Can show (curMax, curMin, best) after each element.

misconceptions.desc: Tracked only the running max, losing the min that becomes max after a negative.
Updated curMax, then used the new curMax to compute curMin (needed a temp).
Did not reset prefix/suffix product after a zero.
Intermediate products overflow int / long long (use long long with resets, or double).

nodes.name: Index-mapped placement
nodes.description: Write each element straight to a computed target index (e.g. positives at even, negatives at odd).

facets.recognize: Sees that the output position of each element is computable on the fly.
facets.implement: Keeps separate next-position indices per group, each stepping by 2.
facets.adapt: Handles unequal group sizes by appending the leftovers.

misconceptions.desc: Used one shared index for both groups.
Variant with unequal counts: leftovers not appended in order.

nodes.name: Boundary (spiral) traversal
nodes.description: Four boundaries (top, bottom, left, right) shrink after each side is printed.

facets.recognize: Uses shrinking boundaries rather than a visited matrix with direction simulation.
facets.explain: Explains why the third and fourth sides need top <= bottom / left <= right guards.
facets.implement: Prints right, down, left, up with correct shrinking and guards.
facets.trace: Can show the four boundaries after each side.

misconceptions.desc: Missing top <= bottom / left <= right checks; single row/column printed twice.
Shrunk the wrong boundary or at the wrong time.
Used a visited matrix (O(mn) extra space) when boundaries suffice.

nodes.name: Transpose & in-place rotation
nodes.description: Rotate 90 degrees clockwise = transpose, then reverse each row.

facets.recognize: Rotates in place instead of building a second matrix.
facets.explain: Explains where (i, j) goes after a transpose and after a row reversal.
facets.implement: Transposes with j > i only, then reverses each row by reference.

misconceptions.desc: Transposed with j starting at 0, so every pair was swapped twice (no change).
Reversed columns instead of rows (rotated the wrong way).
Used a second matrix when in-place was required.

nodes.name: In-place markers (reuse input as storage)
nodes.description: Store flags inside the input (first row/column, sign bits) to reach O(1) extra space.

facets.recognize: Sees that the first row/column can store the row/column flags.
facets.explain: Explains why cell [0][0] needs a separate variable and why the inner cells are processed before the first row/column.
facets.implement: Marks, zeroes the inner cells, then the first row/column, in the right order.

misconceptions.desc: Zeroed the first row/column before using them as markers, wiping the flags.
Used mat[0][0] as the flag for both the first row and the first column.
Marked cells with -1 or another value that can appear in the input.

nodes.name: Pascal's triangle & nCr
nodes.description: Element (r, c) = C(r-1, c-1); rows build from the previous row or from the multiplicative nCr formula.

facets.recognize: Chooses O(c) for one element, O(n) for one row, O(n²) for the whole triangle.
facets.explain: Connects Pascal's triangle to nCr and the previous-row addition rule.
facets.implement: Computes nCr iteratively in long long, multiplying before dividing; builds rows with 1s at both ends.

misconceptions.desc: Computed nCr with factorials (overflows around n = 20).
Divided before multiplying (res = res / (i+1) * (n-i)), introducing truncation.
Mixed 0-based and 1-based row/column numbering (C(r, c) vs C(r-1, c-1)).
Recomputed nCr from scratch for every element of a row (O(n²)) instead of updating from the previous element.

nodes.name: Next lexicographic permutation
nodes.description: Find the breakpoint, swap it with the smallest larger element to its right, reverse the (descending) suffix.

facets.recognize: Avoids generating all permutations.
facets.explain: Explains why the suffix after the breakpoint is descending and why reversing it gives the smallest arrangement.
facets.implement: Finds the breakpoint from the right, swaps with the rightmost larger element, reverses the suffix, handles no breakpoint.
facets.trace: Can show the array after each of the three steps.

misconceptions.desc: Did not handle the fully descending case (reverse the whole array).
Swapped the breakpoint with the wrong element (not the smallest larger one on the right).
Sorted the suffix (O(n log n)) instead of reversing it.
Generated all n! permutations as the approach.

nodes.name: Counting pairs during merge sort
nodes.description: Count cross pairs (i in left, j in right) while both halves are sorted; inversions, reverse pairs.

facets.recognize: Recognizes 'count pairs i < j with a value relation' as divide & conquer.
facets.explain: When left[i] > right[j], every remaining left element also pairs with right[j]: add mid - i + 1.
facets.implement: Counts in long long; for relations that differ from merge order (2x), counts in a separate pass before merging.
facets.adapt: Moves from the inversion condition to a different pair condition (reverse pairs).

misconceptions.desc: Added 1 instead of mid - i + 1 when left[i] > right[j].
Counted reverse pairs inside the merge loop, although the 2x condition differs from the merge order.
Stored the count in int (pair counts reach ~n²/2).
Did not realise the input gets sorted as a side effect.

nodes.name: Merging in place (swap-and-sort / gap method)
nodes.description: Merge two sorted arrays with no extra space: swap the overlapping extremes then sort each, or the shell-sort gap method.

facets.recognize: Recognizes that the no-extra-space constraint rules out the normal merge.
facets.explain: Explains why swapping arr1's largest with arr2's smallest works, and how the gap shrinks with ceil(gap / 2).
facets.implement: Maps a virtual index across both arrays; terminates correctly after gap = 1.

misconceptions.desc: Used gap / 2 (floor) instead of ceil, skipping comparisons or ending early.
Mis-mapped indices across the arr1/arr2 boundary (i >= n means arr2[i - n]).
Used a third array, violating the constraint.
